% ================================================================
% An introduction to indices and roots.
%
% A first sheet on index notation that also builds on algebraic
% notation and on simplifying fractions. Indices are met first with
% integers and decimals, through a match-up of calculations and their
% answers, and then in context through the area of a square and the
% volume of a cube, where the root appears as the operation that
% undoes the index.
%
% The sheet then moves to algebraic variables, writing repeated
% multiplications such as a x a x a over b x b in index form and back
% again. Cancelling a factor found in both the numerator and the
% denominator is taught with integers first, then with a mix of
% integers and variables, and is then used on fractions written with
% indices in a second match-up.
%
% The extension uses the same cancelling on factorials, where most of
% the factors divide out, then asks what happens to powers and roots
% of negative numbers, and ends on the tesseract, the four-dimensional
% shape after the cube, whose corners, hypervolume and edges are all
% counted by powers of 2. Answers are on the last page.
%
% The sheet is written on, so every question is followed by a working
% area. The \newpage commands in the body are placed so that no
% question is split across the fold.
% ================================================================

\pagestyle{empty}
\linespread{1.15}\selectfont

\newcommand{\ansline}[1][2.2cm]{\underline{\hspace{#1}}}
% A short gap for a single number, sized to sit inside a line of maths.
\newcommand{\gap}{\underline{\hspace{0.7cm}}}
% A gap for a number that is written as an index, or on the top or the
% bottom of a fraction. An underline sits too low to be read as an
% index, so a faint dotted box marks where the number is written. The
% size is given in points so that the box does not shrink away when it
% is set as an index.
\newcommand{\boxgap}[1][9pt]{\tikz[baseline=-0.8pt]\draw[gray!60,densely dotted,thick]
  (0,0) rectangle (#1,#1);}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------
% A match-up: calculations in a numbered column on the left, answers in
% a lettered column on the right, with a gap between them for the lines
% pupils draw. The answers are deliberately out of order.
% \matchup[<row spacing>][<column gap>]{<left items>}{<right items>}
% Each item is written inside braces so that it counts as one item.
\newcommand{\mletter}[1]{\ifcase\numexpr#1\relax\or A\or B\or C\or D\or E\or
  F\or G\or H\or I\or J\fi}
\NewDocumentCommand{\matchup}{O{1.1} O{7.2} +m +m}{%
\par\vspace{2pt}\noindent\hfil
\begin{tikzpicture}[mbox/.style={draw=blue!45!black,rounded corners=3pt,thick,
    fill=white,minimum width=2.9cm,minimum height=0.9cm,inner sep=3pt}]
  \foreach [count=\i from 1] \l in {#3} {%
    \node[mbox] (mL\i) at (0,{-#1*\i}) {\l};
    \node[font=\small\bfseries,anchor=east] at ([xshift=-5pt]mL\i.west) {\i.};}
  \foreach [count=\j from 1] \r in {#4} {%
    \node[mbox] (mR\j) at (#2,{-#1*\j}) {\r};
    \node[font=\small\bfseries,anchor=west] at ([xshift=5pt]mR\j.east) {\mletter{\j}};}
\end{tikzpicture}%
\hfil\par\vspace{2pt}}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------
% A 3 by 3 grid of unit squares, which is what 3 squared counts.
\newcommand{\squarepic}{%
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.38]
  \foreach \x in {0,1,2} \foreach \y in {0,1,2}
    \draw[thick,fill=blue!7] (\x,\y) rectangle ++(1,1);
  \draw[<->,>=Stealth,gray!70!black] (0,-0.6) -- (3,-0.6)
    node[midway,below,font=\small,black] {$3$};
  \draw[<->,>=Stealth,gray!70!black] (-0.6,0) -- (-0.6,3)
    node[midway,left,font=\small,black] {$3$};
\end{tikzpicture}}

% A cube of side 2, divided into the 8 unit cubes that 2 cubed counts.
\newcommand{\cubepic}{%
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.52,x={(1cm,0cm)},y={(0.46cm,0.33cm)},z={(0cm,1cm)}]
  \draw[thick,fill=blue!7]  (0,0,0)--(2,0,0)--(2,0,2)--(0,0,2)--cycle;
  \draw[thick,fill=blue!12] (0,0,2)--(2,0,2)--(2,2,2)--(0,2,2)--cycle;
  \draw[thick,fill=blue!16] (2,0,0)--(2,2,0)--(2,2,2)--(2,0,2)--cycle;
  \draw[gray!70!black] (1,0,0)--(1,0,2) (0,0,1)--(2,0,1);
  \draw[gray!70!black] (1,0,2)--(1,2,2) (0,1,2)--(2,1,2);
  \draw[gray!70!black] (2,1,0)--(2,1,2) (2,0,1)--(2,2,1);
  \node[font=\small] at (1,0,-0.5) {$2$};
  \node[font=\small] at (-0.4,0,1) {$2$};
  \node[font=\small] at (2.6,1.2,0) {$2$};
\end{tikzpicture}}

% ----------------------------------------------------------------
% The shapes of the first four dimensions, each drawn with a dot on
% every corner so that the corners can be counted from the picture.
% The dot radius is given in points, so it stays the same size however
% the picture is scaled.
\newcommand{\pointpic}[2]{%
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=#1]
  \fill[blue!45!black] (0,0) circle (#2);
\end{tikzpicture}}
\newcommand{\linepic}[2]{%
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=#1]
  \draw[blue!45!black,thick] (0,0)--(2,0);
  \fill[blue!45!black] (0,0) circle (#2) (2,0) circle (#2);
\end{tikzpicture}}
\newcommand{\squarecorners}[2]{%
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=#1]
  \draw[blue!45!black,thick] (0,0) rectangle (2,2);
  \foreach \a in {0,2} \foreach \b in {0,2} \fill[blue!45!black] (\a,\b) circle (#2);
\end{tikzpicture}}
\newcommand{\cubecorners}[2]{%
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=#1,x={(1cm,0cm)},y={(0.5cm,0.36cm)},z={(0cm,1cm)},
    line join=round]
  \draw[blue!45!black,thick] (0,0,0)--(2,0,0)--(2,2,0)--(0,2,0)--cycle;
  \draw[blue!45!black,thick] (0,0,2)--(2,0,2)--(2,2,2)--(0,2,2)--cycle;
  \draw[blue!45!black,thick] (0,0,0)--(0,0,2) (2,0,0)--(2,0,2)
    (2,2,0)--(2,2,2) (0,2,0)--(0,2,2);
  \foreach \a in {0,2} \foreach \b in {0,2} \foreach \c in {0,2}
    \fill[blue!45!black] (\a,\b,\c) circle (#2);
\end{tikzpicture}}

% A tesseract, drawn the way a cube is drawn on paper: a small cube
% inside a large cube, with every corner of one joined to the matching
% corner of the other. In four dimensions all eight cubes in the
% picture are the same size and all the joining lines are the same
% length, so the picture stretches the shape in the same way that a
% drawing of a cube stretches its square faces.
\newcommand{\tesspic}[2]{%
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=#1,x={(1cm,0cm)},y={(0.5cm,0.36cm)},z={(0cm,1cm)},
    line join=round]
  \foreach \a in {0,4} \foreach \b in {0,4} \foreach \c in {0,4}
    \draw[gray!55] (\a,\b,\c) -- ({1+\a/2},{1+\b/2},{1+\c/2});
  \draw[orange!65!black,thick] (1,1,1)--(3,1,1)--(3,3,1)--(1,3,1)--cycle;
  \draw[orange!65!black,thick] (1,1,3)--(3,1,3)--(3,3,3)--(1,3,3)--cycle;
  \draw[orange!65!black,thick] (1,1,1)--(1,1,3) (3,1,1)--(3,1,3)
    (3,3,1)--(3,3,3) (1,3,1)--(1,3,3);
  \draw[blue!45!black,thick] (0,0,0)--(4,0,0)--(4,4,0)--(0,4,0)--cycle;
  \draw[blue!45!black,thick] (0,0,4)--(4,0,4)--(4,4,4)--(0,4,4)--cycle;
  \draw[blue!45!black,thick] (0,0,0)--(0,0,4) (4,0,0)--(4,0,4)
    (4,4,0)--(4,4,4) (0,4,0)--(0,4,4);
  \foreach \a in {0,4} \foreach \b in {0,4} \foreach \c in {0,4} {%
    \fill[blue!45!black] (\a,\b,\c) circle (#2);
    \fill[orange!65!black] ({1+\a/2},{1+\b/2},{1+\c/2}) circle (#2);}
\end{tikzpicture}}

% a tier 3 word, in English and in translation alike
\newcommand{\ealkey}[1]{\textcolor{ealkeycolour}{#1}}
\newcommand{\ealkeytr}[1]{\textcolor{ealkeycolour}{\ealtext{#1}}}

% One translated word above one English word. Built from kernel
% primitives, never a tabular, which would break wherever the sheet
% loads array, booktabs or tabularx. The box is as wide as the wider of
% the two, so a long translation pushes its neighbours aside instead of
% overlapping them, and it claims its full height so a table row or a
% TikZ node makes room for it.
\newcommand{\ealgloss}[2]{%
  \sbox{\ealboxen}{\ealkey{#1}}%
  \sbox{\ealboxtr}{\small\textcolor{ealtwocolour}{\ealtext{#2}}}%
  \setlength{\ealglosswd}{\wd\ealboxen}%
  \ifdim\wd\ealboxtr>\ealglosswd\setlength{\ealglosswd}{\wd\ealboxtr}\fi
  \leavevmode
  \makebox[\ealglosswd][c]{%
    \makebox[0pt][c]{\usebox{\ealboxen}}%
    \makebox[0pt][c]{\raisebox{\ealglossraise}{\usebox{\ealboxtr}}}%
  }%
}

% opens up line spacing around a block of glosses, so the raised

% a whole translated sentence above its English counterpart. block level,

\newcommand{\ealpara}[2]{%
  \par\addvspace{0.5\baselineskip}%

  \addvspace{0.5\baselineskip}%
}

\begin{document}

\begin{ealglossed}
\begin{center}
  {\Large\bfseries \ealgloss{Indices}{指数} and \ealgloss{Roots}{根}}\\[2pt]
\end{center}
\end{ealglossed}

\begin{keyidea}
\begin{ealglossed}
An \textbf{\ealgloss{index}{指数}} tells us how many times a number is multiplied by itself. So $5^3$ means $5\times5\times5$. The plural
of \ealgloss{index}{指数} is \textbf{\ealgloss{indices}{指数}}. A \textbf{\ealgloss{root}{根}} undoes an \ealgloss{index}{指数}.
\end{ealglossed}
\end{keyidea}

\parttitle{1}{\ealgloss{Indices}{指数} and \ealgloss{roots}{根} of numbers}

\begin{minipage}[t]{0.56\linewidth}
\vspace{0pt}
\begin{ealglossed}
$3^2$ is read ``three \ealgloss{squared}{平方；正方形}''. $2^3$ is read ``two \ealgloss{cubed}{立方}''. 

\vspace{4pt}
The \textbf{\ealgloss{square root}{根}} of a number is the value that gives that number when it (the \ealgloss{square root}{根}) is
multiplied by itself, so $\sqrt{9}=3$. The \textbf{\ealgloss{cube root}{立方根}} of a number is
the value that gives that number when three of them are multiplied together, so
\mbox{$\sqrt[3]{8}=2$}.
\end{ealglossed}
\end{minipage}\hfill
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.41\linewidth}
\vspace{0pt}
\centering
\begin{tabular}{@{}c@{\hspace{0.9em}}c@{}}
\squarepic & \cubepic\\[4pt]
{\small $3^2=3\times3=9$} & {\small $2^3=2\times2\times2=8$}\\
\end{tabular}
\end{minipage}

\vspace{2pt}
\begin{notation}{\ealgloss{indices}{指数} and \ealgloss{roots}{根}}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{2.4}%
\begin{ealglossed}
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\large}p{4.3cm}@{\hspace{0.8em}}p{5.0cm}@{\hspace{0.8em}}l@{}}
$a^2=a\times a$ & ``$a$ \ealgloss{squared}{平方；正方形}'' & for example \; $7^2=7\times7=49$\\
$a^3=a\times a\times a$ & ``$a$ \ealgloss{cubed}{立方}'' & for example \; $2^3=2\times2\times2=8$\\
$\sqrt{a}$ & the \ealgloss{square root}{根} of $a$ & for example \; $\sqrt{49}=7$\\
$\sqrt[3]{a}$ & the \ealgloss{cube root}{立方根} of $a$ & for example \; $\sqrt[3]{8}=2$\\
\end{tabular}

\vspace{2pt}
An \ealgloss{index}{指数} multiplies the \ealgloss{base}{底边} by itself, and a \ealgloss{root}{根} finds the \ealgloss{base}{底边}
again.
\end{ealglossed}
\end{notation}

\begin{enumerate}

\item Work out each calculation on the left and draw a line joining it to
its answer on the right. Check your answers on a calculator afterwards.
\matchup{{$5^2$},{$\sqrt{100}$},{$2^3$},{$0.2^2$},{$\sqrt{0.25}$},{$10^3$},
  {$\sqrt[3]{8}$},{$1.5^2$}}%
  {{$0.5$},{$8$},{$2$},{$25$},{$1000$},{$0.04$},{$2.25$},{$10$}}

\end{enumerate}

\begin{enumerate}[resume]

\item \begin{ealglossed}The shapes are not drawn to \ealgloss{scale}{缩放}.\end{ealglossed}


\begin{enumerate}
  \item \begin{ealglossed}A \ealgloss{square}{平方；正方形} patio has sides of length $6$ m. Work out its \ealgloss{area}{面积}.\end{ealglossed}

\vspace{2pt}
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.34\linewidth}
\centering
\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(current bounding box.north),scale=0.8]
  \draw[thick,fill=blue!6] (0,0) rectangle (2.2,2.2);
  \node[below,font=\small] at (1.1,0) {$6$ m};
  \node[left,font=\small] at (0,1.1) {$6$ m};
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{minipage}%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.62\linewidth}
\vspace{2.2em}
\begin{ealglossed}
\ealgloss{Area}{面积} $=6^2=6\times6=\ansline[1.8cm]$ m$^2$
\end{ealglossed}
\end{minipage}

  \item \begin{ealglossed}A second \ealgloss{square}{平方；正方形} patio has an \ealgloss{area}{面积} of $144$ m$^2$. Work out the length
        of one of its sides.\end{ealglossed}

\vspace{2pt}
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.34\linewidth}
\centering
\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(current bounding box.north),scale=0.8]
  \draw[thick,fill=blue!6] (0,0) rectangle (2.4,2.4);
  \node[font=\small] at (1.2,1.2) {$144$ m$^2$};
  \node[below,font=\small] at (1.2,0) {$?$};
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{minipage}%
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.62\linewidth}
\vspace{1.4em}
Side $=\sqrt{144}=\ansline[1.8cm]$ m
\end{minipage}

  \item \begin{ealglossed}A storage box is a \ealgloss{cube}{立方} with \ealgloss{edges}{棱} of length $4$ cm. Work out its

\vspace{2pt}
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.34\linewidth}

\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(current bounding box.north),scale=0.68,
    x={(1cm,0cm)},y={(0.46cm,0.33cm)},z={(0cm,1cm)}]

  \item \begin{ealglossed}A second storage box is a \ealgloss{cube}{立方} with a \ealgloss{volume}{体积} of $125$ cm$^3$. Work out

  \item \begin{ealglossed}A \ealgloss{square}{平方；正方形} floor tile has an \ealgloss{area}{面积} of $0.25$ m$^2$. Work out the length of
        one of its sides.\end{ealglossed}

\vspace{2pt}
\begin{minipage}[t]{0.34\linewidth}

Side $=\sqrt{0.25}=\ansline[1.8cm]$ m

\parttitle{2}{\ealgloss{Indices}{指数} and \ealgloss{algebraic variables}{变量}}

\begin{ealglossed}
An \textbf{\ealgloss{algebraic variable}{变量}}, such as $a$, $x$ or $m$, could be any number. Just like $5^3=5\times5\times5$, $a^3$ means $a\times a\times a$.
\end{ealglossed}


\begin{warning}
\begin{ealglossed}
In $5a^2$ the \ealgloss{index}{指数} belongs to the $a$ only, so $5a^2=5\times a\times a$. It is
\textbf{not} $5a\times5a$. If $a=2$ then $5a^2=5\times2\times2=20$, but
$5a\times5a=10\times10=100$.
\end{ealglossed}
\end{warning}

\begin{wex}{writing a \ealgloss{fraction}{分数} in \ealgloss{index form}{指数形式}}
\small
\begin{ealglossed}
Write $\dfrac{a\times a\times a}{b\times b}$ in \ealgloss{index form}{指数形式}.
\end{ealglossed}

\smallskip
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{2.4}
\begin{ealglossed}
\begin{tabular}{@{}l@{\hspace{1.2em}}l@{}}
\textbf{Step 1 --- count the \ealgloss{numerator}{分子}.}
  & $a$ appears $3$ times, so the \ealgloss{numerator}{分子} is $a^3$.\\
\textbf{Step 2 --- count the \ealgloss{denominator}{分母}.}
  & $b$ appears $2$ times, so the \ealgloss{denominator}{分母} is $b^2$.\\
\textbf{Step 3 --- write the \ealgloss{fraction}{分数}.}
  & $\dfrac{a\times a\times a}{b\times b}=\dfrac{a^3}{b^2}$\\
\end{tabular}
\end{ealglossed}
\end{wex}


\begin{enumerate}[resume]

\item \begin{ealglossed}Write each \ealgloss{expression}{表达式} in \ealgloss{index form}{指数形式}. Fill in the gaps in parts (a) and
(b), then \ealgloss{simplify}{化简} the remaining \ealgloss{expressions}{表达式} in the same way.\end{ealglossed}
\begin{enumerate}
  \item $a\times a\times a\times a=a^{\boxgap}$
  \item $\dfrac{c\times c\times c}{d\times d}=\dfrac{c^{\boxgap[7pt]}}{d^{\boxgap[7pt]}}$
\end{enumerate}
\vspace{4pt}
\begin{multicols}{3}
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
  \item $b\times b\times b\times b\times b$
  \item $3\times m\times m$
  \item $\dfrac{p\times p\times p}{q\times q\times q\times q}$
  \item $\dfrac{2\times x\times x\times x}{y\times y}$
  \item $\dfrac{a\times a\times b\times b\times b}{c\times c}$
  \item $\dfrac{t\times t}{5\times u\times u\times u}$
\end{enumerate}
\end{multicols}
\vspace{8em}

\item \begin{ealglossed}Write each \ealgloss{expression}{表达式} out in full as a multiplication. The first one is
done for you.\end{ealglossed}
\begin{enumerate}
  \item $x^3=x\times x\times x$
\end{enumerate}
\vspace{2pt}
\begin{multicols}{2}
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
  \item $y^5=\ansline[4cm]$
  \item $4t^2=\ansline[4cm]$
  \item $\dfrac{m^2}{n^3}=\ansline[4cm]$
  \item $\dfrac{a^4}{b}=\ansline[4cm]$
\end{enumerate}
\end{multicols}

\end{enumerate}

\parttitle{3}{\ealgloss{Cancelling}{约分} \ealgloss{factors}{因数} in a \ealgloss{fraction}{分数}}

\begin{ealglossed}
A \ealgloss{fraction}{分数} stays the same
value when the \ealgloss{numerator}{分子} and the \ealgloss{denominator}{分母} are both divided by the same
number. Since the new \ealgloss{fraction}{分数} is \textbf{\ealgloss{equivalent}{等值}} to the original.
\end{ealglossed}

\begin{keyidea}
\begin{ealglossed}
When the \ealgloss{numerator}{分子} and the \ealgloss{denominator}{分母} are written as multiplications, a \ealgloss{factor}{因数}
that appears in both can be divided out of both. This is called
\textbf{\ealgloss{cancelling}{约分}}, and it is written by crossing the \ealgloss{factor}{因数} out on the top
and on the bottom.
\end{ealglossed}
\end{keyidea}

\begin{wex}{\ealgloss{simplify}{化简} $\dfrac{12}{18}$}
\small
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{2.6}
\begin{ealglossed}
\begin{tabular}{@{}l@{\hspace{1.2em}}l@{}}
\textbf{Step 1 --- write the \ealgloss{numerator}{分子} and the \ealgloss{denominator}{分母} as multiplications.}
  & $\dfrac{12}{18}=\dfrac{2\times2\times3}{2\times3\times3}$\\
\textbf{Step 2 --- cross out each \ealgloss{factor}{因数} that appears in both.}
  & $\dfrac{12}{18}=\dfrac{\cancel{2}\times2\times\cancel{3}}
    {\cancel{2}\times\cancel{3}\times3}$\\
\textbf{Step 3 --- multiply what is left on the top and on the bottom.}
  & $\dfrac{12}{18}=\dfrac{2}{3}$\\
\end{tabular}
\end{ealglossed}
\end{wex}

\begin{enumerate}[resume]

\item \begin{ealglossed}\ealgloss{Simplify}{化简} each \ealgloss{fraction}{分数} by \ealgloss{cancelling}{约分}. Fill in the gaps in parts (a) and
(b), then do parts (c) to (f) in the same way.\end{ealglossed}
\begin{enumerate}
  \item $\dfrac{8}{12}=\dfrac{2\times2\times2}{2\times2\times3}
         =\dfrac{\cancel{2}\times\cancel{2}\times2}
          {\cancel{2}\times\cancel{2}\times3}
         =\dfrac{\boxgap[11pt]}{\boxgap[11pt]}$
  \item $\dfrac{15}{25}=\dfrac{5\times3}{5\times\boxgap[11pt]}
         =\dfrac{\boxgap[11pt]}{\boxgap[11pt]}$
\end{enumerate}
\vspace{6pt}
\begin{multicols}{4}
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
  \item $\dfrac{18}{24}$
  \item $\dfrac{14}{21}$
  \item $\dfrac{45}{60}$
  \item $\dfrac{24}{36}$
\end{enumerate}
\end{multicols}
\vspace{6em}

\begin{ealglossed}
\ealgloss{Algebraic variables}{变量} \ealgloss{cancel}{约分} in the same way as numbers. When every \ealgloss{factor}{因数} on the bottom \ealgloss{cancels}{约分}, the \ealgloss{denominator}{分母}
is $1$, not nothing, a \ealgloss{fraction}{分数} with a \ealgloss{denominator}{分母} of $1$ is equal to its
\ealgloss{numerator}{分子}.
\end{ealglossed}

\begin{wex}{\ealgloss{cancelling}{约分} with numbers and variables}
\small
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{2.8}
\begin{ealglossed}
\begin{tabular}{@{}l@{\hspace{1.5em}}l@{}}
$\dfrac{a\times a\times a}{a\times a}
  =\dfrac{\cancel{a}\times\cancel{a}\times a}{\cancel{a}\times\cancel{a}}
  =\dfrac{a}{1}=a$
  & every \ealgloss{factor}{因数} on the bottom \ealgloss{cancels}{约分}, leaving $1$\\
$\dfrac{2\times3\times a\times a}{2\times a}
  =\dfrac{\cancel{2}\times3\times\cancel{a}\times a}
   {\cancel{2}\times\cancel{a}}=\dfrac{3\times a}{1}=3a$
  & the numbers and the variables are \ealgloss{cancelled}{约分} separately\\
\end{tabular}
\end{ealglossed}
\end{wex}

\parttitle{4}{\ealgloss{Simplifying}{化简} \ealgloss{fractions}{分数} written with \ealgloss{indices}{指数}}

\begin{ealglossed}
A \ealgloss{fraction}{分数} written with \ealgloss{indices}{指数} is \ealgloss{simplified}{化简} in the same way. We write each

top and on the bottom, and write what is left in \ealgloss{index form}{指数形式}.
\end{ealglossed}

\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{2.8}

\begin{tabular}{@{}l@{\hspace{2em}}l@{}}
$\dfrac{a^5}{a^2}
  =\dfrac{\cancel{a}\times\cancel{a}\times a\times a\times a}
   {\cancel{a}\times\cancel{a}}=a^3$
  & two of the five $a$s \ealgloss{cancel}{约分}, leaving three\\
$\dfrac{6a^3}{2a}
  =\dfrac{\cancel{2}\times3\times\cancel{a}\times a\times a}
   {\cancel{2}\times\cancel{a}}=3a^2$
  & $6=2\times3$, so a \ealgloss{factor}{因数} of $2$ \ealgloss{cancels}{约分} as well\\
\end{tabular}
\end{ealglossed}
\end{wex}

after it. The \ealgloss{expression}{表达式} $n!$ means multiply together every \ealgloss{whole number}{非负整数} from
$n$ down to $1$, so $5!=5\times4\times3\times2\times1=120$.

$10!=10\times9\times8\times7\times6\times5\times4\times3\times2\times1=3\,628\,800$.

\item \begin{ealglossed}A \ealgloss{square}{平方；正方形} is the two-\ealgloss{dimensional}{尺寸} shape made by sliding a line at \ealgloss{right angles}{直角}
to itself, a \ealgloss{cube}{立方} is the three-\ealgloss{dimensional}{尺寸} shape made by sliding a
\ealgloss{square}{平方；正方形} at \ealgloss{right angles}{直角} to itself. A \textbf{\ealgloss{tesseract}{四维超立方体}} is the shape made by
sliding a \ealgloss{cube}{立方} at \ealgloss{right angles}{直角} to itself, in the fourth direction. There is no
fourth direction in the space we live in, so a \ealgloss{tesseract}{四维超立方体} cannot be built, but
it can still be drawn and its measurements can still be worked out.\end{ealglossed}

\textbf{Q1.} 1--D ($25$) \quad 2--H ($10$) \quad 3--B ($8$) \quad
4--F ($0.04$) \quad 5--A ($0.5$) \quad 6--E ($1000$) \quad 7--C ($2$) \quad
8--G ($2.25$)

\textbf{Q2.} (a) $6\times6=36$ m$^2$ \quad (b) $\sqrt{144}=12$ m \quad
(c) $4\times4\times4=64$ cm$^3$ \quad (d) $\sqrt[3]{125}=5$ cm \quad
(e) $\sqrt{0.25}=0.5$ m \quad (f) Between $7$ m and $8$ m, because
$7^2=49$ and $8^2=64$, and $50$ is between $49$ and $64$.

\textbf{Q3.} (a) $a^4$ \quad (b) $\dfrac{c^3}{d^2}$ \quad (c) $b^5$ \quad
(d) $3m^2$ \quad (e) $\dfrac{p^3}{q^4}$ \quad (f) $\dfrac{2x^3}{y^2}$ \quad
(g) $\dfrac{a^2b^3}{c^2}$ \quad (h) $\dfrac{t^2}{5u^3}$

\textbf{Q4.} (b) $y\times y\times y\times y\times y$ \quad
(c) $4\times t\times t$ \quad (d) $\dfrac{m\times m}{n\times n\times n}$ \quad
(e) $\dfrac{a\times a\times a\times a}{b}$

\textbf{Q5.} (a) $\dfrac{2}{3}$ \quad
(b) $\dfrac{5\times3}{5\times5}=\dfrac{3}{5}$ \quad (c) $\dfrac{3}{4}$ \quad
(d) $\dfrac{2}{3}$ \quad (e) $\dfrac{3}{4}$ \quad (f) $\dfrac{2}{3}$ \quad
(g) $\dfrac{12}{28}=\dfrac{3}{7}$ \quad (h) $\dfrac{45}{120}=\dfrac{3}{8}$

\begin{ealglossed}
\textbf{Q6.} (a) $a^2$ \quad (b) $b^3$ \quad (c) $2m$ \quad (d) $3p^2$ \quad
(e) $\dfrac{x}{y}$ \quad (f) $\dfrac{2t}{3}$ \quad (g) $\dfrac{2x}{3y}$
\quad (h) $\dfrac{5b}{a}$ \quad (i) Two $a$s \ealgloss{cancel}{约分} from the top and the
bottom, which leaves $1$ on the top and one $a$ on the bottom. Lena has put the
$a$ that is left on the top. The answer is $\dfrac{1}{a}$.
\end{ealglossed}

\textbf{Q7.} 1--D ($a^3$) \quad 2--F ($1$) \quad 3--H ($3a^2$) \quad
4--G ($a^2$) \quad 5--E ($\frac{a}{2}$) \quad 6--A ($b^2$) \quad
7--C ($2$) \quad 8--B ($a^4$)

\begin{ealglossed}
\textbf{Q8.} (a) There are many answers, for example $\dfrac{2a^3}{a}$, \;
$\dfrac{4a^3}{2a}$ \; and \; $\dfrac{6a^5}{3a^3}$. \quad (b) There are many
answers, for example $\dfrac{a^3}{ab}$ or $\dfrac{a^2b}{b^2}$. \quad
(c) There are many answers, for example $\dfrac{z}{xy^2z}$ or
$\dfrac{xz}{x^2y^2z}$. \quad (d) \ealgloss{Cancelling}{约分} divides the top and the bottom by the same \ealgloss{factor}{因数}, and a number
divided by itself is $1$, not $0$. What is left on the top is $1$ and what is
left on the bottom is $1$, so $\dfrac{3a^2}{3a^2}=\dfrac{1}{1}=1$.
\end{ealglossed}

\begin{ealglossed}
\textbf{Q9.} (a) $a^4$, \; $b^5$, \; $c$ \quad (b) Subtract the \ealgloss{index}{指数} on the
bottom from the \ealgloss{index}{指数} on the top, and keep the same \ealgloss{base}{底边}. \quad
(c) $x^7$, \; $y$ \quad (d) $\dfrac{a^3}{a^3}=a^{3-3}=a^0$, and \ealgloss{cancelling}{约分}
gives $1$, so $a^0=1$.
\end{ealglossed}

\textbf{Q10.} (a) $6$ \quad (b) $24$ \quad (c) $720$ \quad (d) $1$

\textbf{Q11.} (a) $5\times4=20$ \quad (b) $10$ \quad (c) $8\times7=56$ \quad
(d) $\dfrac{7\times6}{2\times1}=21$ \quad (e) $100\times99=9900$ \quad
(f) $\dfrac{12\times11}{2\times1}=66$

\begin{ealglossed}
\textbf{Q12.} $n!=n\times(n-1)\times(n-2)\times\cdots\times1$ and
$(n-1)!=(n-1)\times(n-2)\times\cdots\times1$. Every \ealgloss{factor}{因数} of $(n-1)!$ also
appears in $n!$, so all of them \ealgloss{cancel}{约分}. The only \ealgloss{factor}{因数} left on the top is $n$,
and the bottom is $1$.
\end{ealglossed}

\begin{ealglossed}
\textbf{Q13.} (a) $(-2)^3=-8$; \;
$(-2)^4=(-2)\times(-2)\times(-2)\times(-2)=16$; \;
$(-3)^2=(-3)\times(-3)=9$; \; $(-3)^3=(-3)\times(-3)\times(-3)=-27$. \quad
(b) An \ealgloss{even}{偶数的} \ealgloss{index}{指数} gives a \ealgloss{positive}{正数} answer and an \ealgloss{odd}{奇数} \ealgloss{index}{指数} gives a \ealgloss{negative}{负的}
answer. \quad (c) Two \ealgloss{negative}{负的} numbers multiplied together give a \ealgloss{positive}{正数}
answer, so the \ealgloss{negative}{负的} \ealgloss{signs}{正负号} pair up. An \ealgloss{even}{偶数的} \ealgloss{index}{指数} leaves no \ealgloss{negative}{负的} \ealgloss{sign}{正负号}
over, and an \ealgloss{odd}{奇数} \ealgloss{index}{指数} leaves one \ealgloss{negative}{负的} \ealgloss{sign}{正负号} over.
\end{ealglossed}

\begin{ealglossed}
\textbf{Q14.} (a) $3\times3=9$ and $(-3)\times(-3)=9$, so the two numbers are
$3$ and $-3$. \quad (b) The calculator shows an error. No number multiplied by
itself gives a \ealgloss{negative}{负的} answer, because a \ealgloss{positive}{正数} multiplied by a \ealgloss{positive}{正数} is
\ealgloss{positive}{正数}, and a \ealgloss{negative}{负的} multiplied by a \ealgloss{negative}{负的} is also \ealgloss{positive}{正数}. \quad
(c) $(-2)\times(-2)\times(-2)=-8$, so $\sqrt[3]{-8}=-2$. \quad (d) Sam is not
right. A \ealgloss{negative}{负的} number has no \ealgloss{square root}{根}, because an \ealgloss{even}{偶数的} \ealgloss{index}{指数} always gives
a \ealgloss{positive}{正数} answer, but it does have a \ealgloss{cube root}{立方根}, because an \ealgloss{odd}{奇数} \ealgloss{index}{指数} can give
a \ealgloss{negative}{负的} answer.
\end{ealglossed}

\begin{ealglossed}
\textbf{Q15.} (a) The \ealgloss{cube}{立方} has $8$ corners and the \ealgloss{tesseract}{四维超立方体} has $16$
corners. \quad (b) \ealgloss{Square}{平方；正方形}: $4=2^2$; \; \ealgloss{cube}{立方}: $8=2^3$; \; \ealgloss{tesseract}{四维超立方体}:
$16=2^4$. The \ealgloss{index}{指数} is the number of \ealgloss{dimensions}{尺寸}. \quad
(c) $2^5=32$ corners \quad (d) $1024=2^{10}$, so it has $10$ \ealgloss{dimensions}{尺寸}. \quad
(e) $3^4=3\times3\times3\times3=81$ cm$^4$ \quad
(f) $\sqrt[4]{16}=2$ cm, because $2\times2\times2\times2=16$. \quad
(g) $(-2)\times(-2)\times(-2)\times(-2)=16$, because the \ealgloss{index}{指数} is \ealgloss{even}{偶数的}. The
\ealgloss{edge}{棱} must still be $2$ cm, because a length cannot be \ealgloss{negative}{负的}. \quad
(h) $\sqrt[4]{81}=3$ cm, because $3\times3\times3\times3=81$. \quad
(i) \ealgloss{Square}{平方；正方形}: $4=2\times2^1$; \; \ealgloss{tesseract}{四维超立方体}: $32=4\times2^3$. The number in front
is the number of \ealgloss{dimensions}{尺寸} and the \ealgloss{index}{指数} is one less than it, so the
five-\ealgloss{dimensional}{尺寸} shape has $5\times2^4=80$ \ealgloss{edges}{棱}. \quad
(j) Corners $=2^6=64$; \; \ealgloss{edges}{棱} $=6\times2^5=192$.
\end{ealglossed}

\end{multicols}
